question: The distance between two electric poles of length 25 metres and 36 metres is x metres. If the two angles of elevation of their respective top from the bottom of the other are complementary to each other, then the value of x (in metres) is:
solution:
**Given:**

Length of pole 1 = 25 metres

Length of pole 2 = 36 metres

Angles of elevation are complementary

**Formula Used:**

tan(θ) × tan(90° − θ) = 1

tan(θ) = height/distance

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/178d2377885455f19c9e8b5c0433f7b878ced8f1b9a46f3167a6b0d70340ad70.png] 

Let the distance between the poles be x metres.

tan(θ) = 25/x

tan(90° − θ) = 36/x

tan(θ) × tan(90° − θ) = 1

⇒ (25/x) × (36/x) = 1

⇒ 900/x² = 1

⇒ x² = 900

⇒ x = √900

⇒ x = 30

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**
